Class Dropdown<T>

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.core.AbstractPanelElement<Dropdown<T>>
com.trevlar.menukit.core.Dropdown<T>
Type Parameters:
T - selection value type; identity via T.equals()
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public final class Dropdown<T> extends AbstractPanelElement<Dropdown<T>>
Single-selection dropdown control. Phase 14d-5 — bespoke composition (no vanilla wrap; vanilla 26.2 ships CycleButton which cycles in place, but no popover-list dropdown widget). Owns trigger render + popover render + click routing internally; new PanelElement.hitTest(double, double, int, int) primitive lets the popover area receive clicks despite rendering outside the trigger's layout bounds.

The architectural patterns inherited from vanilla are not a widget wrap but the host-screen-owns-dispatch pattern from CommandSuggestions / SuggestionsList (chat command autocomplete) plus the edge-flip placement pattern from BelowOrAboveWidgetTooltipPositioner. Heuristic 6 (follow vanilla) applied at the pattern level rather than the widget level.

Lens pattern (Principle 8) — Supplier+Consumer over T

Generic-typed lens pair. Library reads supplier each frame to render the current selection in the trigger label; library calls consumer when the user picks an item from the popover. Selection identity via T.equals(). null supplier values OK — trigger renders the empty placeholder.

Per-frame supplier-pull is idempotent: Dropdown stores no value internally — the supplier IS the source of truth. Programmatic resets (server sync, reset-to-default) work transparently — consumer changes its own state, next frame the trigger label updates.

No imperative setValue(T) escape hatch (matches Slider / ScrollContainer; consumer-as-source-of-truth eliminates the "library holds state, consumer pushes in" gap).

API surface

Dropdown<GameMode> dropdown = Dropdown.<GameMode>builder()
    .at(0, 0)
    .triggerSize(120, 20)
    .items(List.of(GameMode.SURVIVAL, GameMode.CREATIVE, GameMode.ADVENTURE))
    .label(gm -> Component.literal(gm.name()))
    .selection(() -> currentMode, m -> currentMode = m)
    .maxVisibleItems(8)            // optional; default 8
    .build();
Same label function does double duty: trigger shows label.apply(currentSelection); popover items show label.apply(item) per row (matches vanilla CycleButton's single-stringifier shape).

Popover placement — auto edge-flip

Open direction is determined at open time:
  • Default: below trigger (popover renders at triggerY + triggerHeight).
  • If trigger sits low enough that triggerY + triggerHeight + popoverHeight overflows screen.height, popover flips above (triggerY - popoverHeight).
  • Popover X-axis: left-aligns with trigger; clamps to screen.width - popoverWidth so the right edge stays on-screen (matches the Mth.clamp pattern from CommandSuggestions).
No .openDirection() builder option in v1; AUTO only. Defer override to evidence per the principle of fold-on-evidence.

Render-overlay z-order (Phase 18t)

The popover renders via renderOverlay(RenderContext) — the second pass PanelDispatch.renderElements(Panel, RenderContext) runs after every element's base render(RenderContext). Result: an open popover always paints on top of every sibling element regardless of declaration order. Consumers no longer need to declare Dropdowns LAST — any order works.

The one residual ordering rule: when multiple Dropdowns are open simultaneously (rare — typically only one popover is open at a time), later-declared Dropdowns' popovers paint over earlier-declared ones, because renderOverlay iterates in declaration order too. In the common single-open case this is invisible.

Cross-context applicability

  • MenuContext (inventory menus): yes — settings panels, enum selectors.
  • StandaloneContext (MKScreen): yes — full-screen MenuKit-native UIs.
  • SlotGroupContext: no — slot-group anchors are for slot decorations only.
  • HudContext: no — HUDs are render-only (no input dispatch); Dropdown's defining feature is interactive selection.

What v1 does NOT do (deferred)

  • Multi-select / search-as-you-type — separate primitives.
  • Keyboard nav (arrows / Enter / Esc) — no vanilla widget to inherit from; bespoke implementation deferred. Esc still closes the parent screen via vanilla's standard handling.
  • Programmatic open/close — open is internal state per the Slider dragging precedent.
  • Custom item rendering (icons, multi-line) — v1 ships single-line text rows via label.apply(item).
  • Dynamic items list — items is immutable post-build; dynamic items is a separate primitive (Combobox / Autocomplete).

    • getHeight

      public int getHeight()
      Trigger height — grows when the selection label wraps to more than one line (Verification-4 reactive wrap, mirroring TextLabel). Authored triggerHeight is the floor: a wrapped trigger is at least its authored box, and grows to topPad + lineCount*lineHeight + botPad when the label spans multiple lines. Single-line (the common case) returns the authored height unchanged.

      Reversible: the wrapped line count is recomputed from font.split(label, textAreaW) every frame against the LIVE trigger width, so a later wider layoutWithin(int) budget collapses the label back to one line and this returns to triggerHeight.

    • layoutWithin

      public void layoutWithin(int budget)
      Cap the trigger to the panel's budget so it never bleeds; reversible. An over-long selected value WRAPS within the trigger (see renderTriggerContent(GuiGraphicsExtractor, int, int) + getHeight()), not scroll.
      Parameters:
      budget - horizontal pixels available to this element, in panel content space. Always >= 1.

    • extraLayoutHeight

      public int extraLayoutHeight()
      Extra vertical pixels the trigger occupies BEYOND its authored box because the selection label wrapped — getHeight() - triggerHeight when wrapped, else 0. The owning Panel reflows the elements below this Dropdown downward by exactly this amount, so a label that grows from one line to two pushes — never paints over — what's beneath it (mirrors TextLabel.extraLayoutHeight). The popover already anchors off the LIVE trigger height via computePopoverBounds(int, int), so it follows the growth automatically with no extra wiring.

    • getActiveOverlayBounds

      public int @Nullable [] getActiveOverlayBounds()
      Phase 14d-5 active-overlay claim — when popover is open, declares the popover's screen-space bounds as an exclusive modal-area. The dispatcher routes ALL clicks (and scrolls) inside the popover bounds solely to this Dropdown, regardless of mouseClicked(double, double, int)'s return — elements behind the popover (including any Button or vanilla widget visually occluded by it) stay innately inert.

      This is the parallel to M9's panel-level modal click-eat at the element level. Without it, a click on a popover item would also fire whichever element's layout bounds happened to overlap the popover region (e.g., a Reset button paint-occluded by an edge-flipped popover).

      Trigger bounds are NOT included in the overlay — the trigger dispatches via the standard PanelElement.hitTest(double, double, int, int) pass (default = layout bounds). When the popover is closed, returns null so no overlay is active.

      Returns:
      [x, y, width, height] of the active overlay region, or null if no overlay is active

    • renderOverlay

      public void renderOverlay(RenderContext ctx)
      Phase 18s follow-up — popover renders on the overlay pass so it always wins z-order regardless of consumer element-declaration order. Pairs with getActiveOverlayBounds() for the input- side exclusive claim — together they make the open popover both visually on top AND inert-to-anything-underneath.

      Uses the trigger screen-position cached during the base render(RenderContext) pass (renderOverlay runs in the same frame, so the cache is fresh).

      Parameters:
      ctx - per-frame render context, same instance passed to PanelElement.render(RenderContext) on the base pass

    • mouseClicked

      public boolean mouseClicked(double mouseX, double mouseY, int button)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Called when the mouse is clicked on this element. The dispatcher hit-tests against the element's bounds before calling this method, so implementations know the click is within bounds.

      Returns true if this element consumed the click (preventing further dispatch to slots or vanilla). The default returns false, so render-only elements (TextLabel, Icon, ItemDisplay) don't need to override it.

      The button parameter is the mouse button: 0=left, 1=right, 2=middle. Core Button only consumes left-click; custom elements can handle any button.

      Parameters:
      mouseX - screen-space mouse X
      mouseY - screen-space mouse Y
      button - mouse button (0=left, 1=right, 2=middle)
      Returns:
      true if consumed, false to let the click fall through

    • notifyClickOutsideOverlay

      public void notifyClickOutsideOverlay(double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Outside-click dismiss — closes the open popover when a click lands outside BOTH the popover and the trigger. The dispatcher calls this on every visible element for a click it didn't route into the element (so it fires even when another element consumed the click), making "click away to close" work the way every native popup does. In-trigger clicks (toggle) and in-popover clicks (item pick) are handled by mouseClicked(double, double, int) via the hit-test / overlay passes, and are no-ops here.
      Parameters:
      mouseX - screen-space x of the click that fell outside all claims
      mouseY - screen-space y of the click that fell outside all claims

    • mouseScrolled

      public boolean mouseScrolled(double mouseX, double mouseY, double scrollX, double scrollY)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Called when the user scrolls the mouse wheel with the cursor over this element's bounds. The container hit-tests before calling — implementations know the cursor is within bounds.

      Returns true if this element consumed the scroll (preventing further dispatch). Default returns false, so non-scrollable elements (Button, TextLabel, etc.) don't need to override it.

      scrollX / scrollY are the wheel deltas — typically scrollY is non-zero (vertical wheel) and scrollX is zero (horizontal wheel, less common).

      Added in Phase 14d-2 alongside ScrollContainer, the first element that consumes scroll input. Existing elements default false and continue to work unchanged.

      Parameters:
      mouseX - screen-space mouse X
      mouseY - screen-space mouse Y
      scrollX - horizontal wheel delta (typically 0)
      scrollY - vertical wheel delta (positive = up, negative = down)
      Returns:
      true if consumed, false to let the scroll fall through

    • keyPressed

      public boolean keyPressed(int keyCode, int scanCode, int modifiers)
      Keyboard navigation — the keyboard counterpart to mouseClicked(double, double, int), completing the dropdown's input model. Scoped to the OPEN popover: a closed dropdown returns false and consumes nothing, because there is no keyboard-focus model to arbitrate which of several on-screen dropdowns owns a key — opening stays mouse-driven, and a closed dropdown never swallows a sibling's or vanilla's keystroke.
      • Up / Down — move the highlighted row (the first press reveals the highlight at the current selection); auto-scrolls to keep it visible.
      • Enter — select the highlighted row and close.
      • Escape — close the popover (consumed, so the underlying screen stays open: Esc dismisses the dropdown first).
      Parameters:
      keyCode - GLFW key code
      scanCode - platform-specific scan code
      modifiers - GLFW modifier bitfield (shift/ctrl/alt)
      Returns:
      true if consumed, false to let the key fall through
